newsitem.title: LEBANON: Pope likely to visit Lebanon in May, envoy says.
newsitem.headline: Pope likely to visit Lebanon in May, envoy says.

text.p: Pope John Paul, who cancelled a visit to Lebanon in 1994 due to security risks, will probably visit the Middle Eastern country for up to 48 hours in May, papal nuncio Pablo Puente said on Thursday.
The visit would be to Lebanon only, not including any other Middle Eastern country, the Vatican diplomat told reporters.

The Vatican indefinitely postponed a five-day papal visit to Lebanon scheduled for May 1994 after the bombing of a Maronite church north of Beirut three months earlier that killed 11 Sunday worshippers and injured 59.

Asked about reports from the Vatican that the pope would now make a 36-hour visit to Lebanon on May 10 or 11, Puente said: "Do not ask me about the date of the visit. There is no official announcement in this regard but this is the most probable...
"All I can say is that if the visit takes place it will be for 24 to 48 hours ...," he added.
"The pope will stay at our embassy. His visit will include a tour of (the biblical cities of) Tyre and Sidon as we consider the south a sacred land."
Asked if the pope would visit other countries in the region, Puente said: "No, he will visit Lebanon and then leave straight for Rome."
